note.explanation: In physics, work is done when a force moves an object through a distance. Only the part of the force in the direction of the object's motion does work. Work is measured in joules.
examples: A force of 10 N moves an object 3 m in the same direction: W = FS = 10 × 3 = 30 J.
A person carries a bag horizontally at a steady height. The supporting force is vertical and the displacement is horizontal, so the work done by that force is zero.
note.checkAnswer: Zero joules; the force and displacement are perpendicular.
note.simple: A force does work only when it moves something in the force's direction. A force sideways to the motion, or no movement at all, means no work by that force.
note.checkQuestion: A force holds a bag upward while the bag moves horizontally. How much work does this force do?
note.title: Work done by a force
steps: Identify the force, the distance moved and the angle between them.
Use W = FS when the force and displacement are in the same direction.
Use W = FS cos θ when the force makes an angle θ with the direction of motion.
note.answer: Work is the product of the magnitude of force and the distance covered in the direction of force.

mcqs.stem: A force of 4 N moves an object 3 m in the direction of the force. How much work is done?
rationales: This is correct because W = FS = 4 × 3 = 12 J.
This is incorrect because it does not equal the product of force and distance.
This is incorrect because the object moves in the direction of the applied force.
This is incorrect because it multiplies by an extra factor of 4.

options: The object has a large mass
The force acts for a long time
mcqs.stem: A force acts on an object, but the object does not move. What is the work done by that force?
rationales: This is incorrect because a force can be non-zero even when no work is done.
This is correct because W = FS, and zero displacement makes the work zero.
This is incorrect because mass alone does not determine work.
This is incorrect because time alone does not determine work in this definition.

mcqs.stem: A force F acts at an angle θ to the direction of motion over distance S. Which expression gives the work done?
rationales: This is incorrect unless the force is entirely along the direction of motion.
This is incorrect because the component along the motion is F cos θ.
This is correct because only the force component F cos θ acts along the displacement.
This is incorrect because force divided by distance is not work.

mcqs.stem: A force acts perpendicular to an object's displacement. What is the work done by this force?
rationales: This is correct because cos 90° = 0 in W = FS cos θ.
This is incorrect because it would apply if force and displacement were in the same direction.
This is incorrect because work is not the sum of force and distance.
This is incorrect because force divided by distance is not work.

mcqs.stem: What is the SI unit of work?
rationales: This is incorrect because a newton is the SI unit of force.
This is correct because the SI unit of work is the joule (J).
This is incorrect because a metre is a unit of distance.
This is incorrect because a watt is a unit of power.

options: The slope of a force-distance graph
The area under a force-distance graph
The highest force shown on the graph
mcqs.stem: For a force-distance graph, what represents the work done by the force?
rationales: This is incorrect because the slope does not generally give the work.
This is correct because the area under the force-distance curve represents work done.
This is incorrect because force alone does not include the distance moved.
This is incorrect because distance alone does not include the force.

written.text: A person does 200 J of work in pushing a carton through a distance of 5 metres. How much force is applied by him?

rubric.why: The correct work equation must be selected and rearranged.
rubric.description: Use and rearrange the work equation.
rubric.how: Write W = F × S, so F = W/S.

rubric.why: The given values must be substituted correctly.
rubric.how: Put W = 200 J and S = 5 m into F = W/S.

rubric.why: The numerical result and its unit complete the answer.

modelAnswer: Work done W = 200 J; distance S = 5 m.
From W = F × S, F = W/S.

written.text: Find the work done by a 65 N force in pulling the suitcase (Fig. 5.8) for a distance of 20 metres.

rubric.why: The force, distance and angle from the figure are needed.
rubric.how: State F = 65 N, S = 20 m and θ = 30°.

rubric.why: The angled-force equation accounts for the component along the motion.
Correct substitution and use of cos 30° are required.
The final value and joule unit state the work done.

modelAnswer: Force applied F = 65 N; distance covered S = 20 m; θ = 30°.

written.text: What is the work done on an object that remains at rest when a force is applied on it?
written.finalAnswer: Zero work is done because the displacement is zero.

rubric.why: The work is zero when the object does not move.
rubric.how: Answer that the work done is zero.

rubric.why: The explanation connects the result to W = FS.
rubric.how: State that the displacement is zero.

modelAnswer: Since the object remains at rest, S = 0.

written.text: Define work and its SI unit.
written.finalAnswer: Work is the product of the magnitude of force and the distance covered in the direction of force. Its SI unit is the joule (J).

rubric.why: The definition must include force and distance in the force's direction.
rubric.how: Give the textbook definition of work.

rubric.why: The SI unit is an essential part of the answer.

modelAnswer: Work is the product of the magnitude of force and the distance covered in the direction of force.
The SI unit of work is joule (J).

written.text: A man rowing boat upstream is at rest with respect to the shore. Is he doing work?
written.finalAnswer: No mechanical work is done on the boat because it has no displacement with respect to the shore.

rubric.why: The answer must decide whether work is done on the boat.
rubric.how: Say no mechanical work is done on the boat.

rubric.why: Work depends on displacement of the object in the question.
rubric.how: State that the boat has no displacement relative to the shore.

rubric.why: The work equation shows why zero displacement gives zero work.
rubric.description: Connect the explanation to the equation.

modelAnswer: The boat is at rest with respect to the shore, so its displacement S = 0.
Therefore, no mechanical work is done on the boat.

written.text: A force of 20 N acting at an angle of 60° to the horizontal is used to pull a box through a distance of 3 m across a floor. How much work is done?

rubric.why: The force is at an angle to the displacement.
All given values must be placed in the equation.
rubric.how: Use F = 20 N, S = 3 m and θ = 60°.

rubric.why: The cosine of the angle gives the force component along the motion.
The correct work value and unit are the final result.

written.text: A body moves a distance of 5 metres in a straight line under the action of a force of 8 newtons. If the work done is 20 joules, find the angle which the force makes with the direction of motion of the body.

rubric.why: The angled-force equation relates work to the unknown angle.
rubric.how: Start with W = FS cos θ.

rubric.why: Correct substitution and rearrangement are needed to find the angle.
This value identifies the angle through the cosine ratio.
The angle must be stated as the final answer.

written.text: A person pushes a lawn mower with a force of 50 N making an angle of 45° with the horizontal. If the mower is moved through a distance of 20 m, how much work is done?

rubric.why: The force is inclined to the direction of motion.
Substitution must use the stated force, distance and angle.
The cosine gives the component of the force along the horizontal displacement.
The final work value and unit complete the numerical answer.

written.text: Calculate the work done in (i) Pushing a 5 kg box up a frictionless inclined plane 10 m long that makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal.

rubric.why: The component of the box's weight along the plane determines the force needed.
rubric.description: Find the force along the plane.
rubric.how: Use F = mg sin 30° = 25 N, taking g = 10 m/s².

rubric.why: The force and motion are along the plane.
The force and distance must be substituted correctly.
rubric.how: Use F = 25 N and S = 10 m.

rubric.why: The correct work and unit give the required result.

modelAnswer: Force along the plane F = mg sin 30°.

written.text: Calculate the work done in (ii) Lifting the box vertically up from the ground to the top of the inclined plane.

rubric.why: The vertical height is needed for the lifting distance.
The lifting force equals the box's weight.
Work is force multiplied by vertical distance here.
The final work and unit complete the answer.

modelAnswer: Force needed F = mg = 5 kg × 10 m/s² = 50 N.

written.text: A force F acts through a distance L on a body. The force is then increased to 2F that further acts through 2L. Sketch a force-displacement graph and calculate the total work done.

rubric.why: Work is represented by the area under a force-distance graph.
rubric.how: State that work equals the area under the force-displacement graph.

rubric.why: The first constant-force section contributes an area FL.
The second section contributes work at force 2F over distance 2L.
Adding both areas gives the total work.

modelAnswer: Work done is the area under the force-displacement graph.
First part: W₁ = F × L = FL.
Total work = W₁ + W₂ = FL + 4FL = 5FL or 5 units.

examTips: A short-answer question may ask for the definition of work or its SI unit. Include both force and distance in the force's direction in the definition.
Numerical questions commonly give force, distance and sometimes an angle. Write W = FS for the same direction, or W = FS cos θ for an angled force, then substitute values and include J.
For a force-distance graph, the work is the area under the graph. For a constant force, this area is a rectangle of area F × S.
State clearly when work is zero: either there is no displacement or the force is perpendicular to the displacement.

hints: The force is not in the same direction as the box's motion.
Use W = FS cos θ, with cos 60° = 0.5.

explain.title: When is work done?
explain.body: Work is said to be done when a force acts on an object and moves it through some distance. The textbook defines work as: “Work is defined as the product of magnitude of force and the distance covered in the direction of force.”

explain.title: Work in the same direction
explain.body: When force and distance are in the same direction, use W = F × S. If an object does not move, its displacement is zero and no work is done by the force.

explain.title: A force at an angle
explain.body: Only the component F cos θ acts along the motion. Therefore, W = FS cos θ. At 90°, cos 90° = 0, so a perpendicular force does no work.

explain.title: Work, graphs and units
explain.body: Work is a scalar quantity, so it has magnitude but no direction. The area under a force-distance graph represents work. The SI unit is the joule: 1 J = 1 N m.

mistakes: Using W = FS when the force is at an angle; use W = FS cos θ instead.
Using the full force instead of its component along the displacement.
Saying that work is done simply because a force is applied, even when there is no displacement.
Forgetting that a perpendicular force does zero work.
Leaving out the unit J, or writing the wrong unit for work.
Treating work as a vector; work is a scalar quantity.
